# Set up an agent operating model

Generate a project's agent operating model: a main session acting as CEO, leads per area, specialists, a fixed report format, per-task model and effort rules with a floor in every agent file, a review cadence, and per-area practices for how agents work on each kind of thing. Read, ask little, propose once, write after one "yes".

## Step 1 — Read the project

Collect signals and record the path each came from. The list and how to count areas are in [references/sizing-signals.md](references/sizing-signals.md). Count code volume with a command that prints totals (`find … | wc -l` style), never by reading files. Read, when present: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PRD.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and the user's `CLAUDE.md` if it is reachable.

If `.claude/agents/` or an `OPERATING-MODEL.md` already exists, switch to update mode: follow [references/update-mode.md](references/update-mode.md) for every later step.

Count recent commits (for example `git log --since="8 weeks ago" --oneline`) to set the periodic review's frequency: weekly at 8 or more commits in that window, every two weeks at 3–7, monthly at 2 or fewer.

From the `CLAUDE.md` files, note what the environment already decides and inherit it instead of inventing it:

- **Language.** The owner's language sets the language of reports, questions and headings, and the agent file names: Portuguese → `lider-<area>.md` / `especialista-<tarefa>.md`; any other → `lead-<area>.md` / `specialist-<task>.md`.
- **Shell and context tooling rules.** If a `CLAUDE.md` already has rules for shell commands or for reading files, the protocol points at them; never copy them. If none exist, write nothing about it.
- **Owner working style.** Use the environment's own and never override it. Offer the items of [references/owner-working-style.md](references/owner-working-style.md) that it does not settle in Step 4, each off until the owner turns it on.

## Step 2 — Size the model

Count justified areas and pick the tier from the table in [references/sizing-signals.md](references/sizing-signals.md): Small (1–2, no leads), Medium (3–5), Large (6+). Code volume only breaks a tie at a boundary. Every area and every agent must trace to a signal; drop anything that doesn't. **Each lead owns exactly one area and each specialist does one kind of work:** never merge areas into one lead or kinds of work into one specialist. An area the owner names in answer to question 2 counts, with ``Signal: `owner answer, question 2` `` (or its ROADMAP path).

Map the justified areas to their practices files (`docs/practices/<area>.md`: how agents work on screens, APIs, deploys, security, legal texts, marketing, product) with the table in [references/practices.md](references/practices.md).

## Step 3 — Ask at most three questions

Only what the repo cannot show, one question per message, multiple choice, your inferred answer first as the recommendation. **Skip any question the request already answers**; if all three are answered, go straight to the proposal.

1. Who the human owner is: one person or a team.
2. Areas planned that have no code yet.
3. What must never happen without the owner (extends the owner-only list).

Every other open point goes into the proposal as an editable default — never a fourth question.

## Step 4 — Propose, in one message

Use this shape so it can be checked line by line, in the owner's language for prose but with these literal keys:

```
Tier: <Small|Medium|Large> (<N> justified areas)
Chain of command: owner → main session → <leads → >specialists

Areas
- <area> — <one line>. Signal: `<path>`

Agents
- <file name> (<lead|specialist|reviewer>, model <alias> / effort <level>) — <one line>. Signal: `<path>`

Editable defaults
- Worktrees: one per task branch, created by the dispatcher (change to read-only if your tooling refuses `git` there)
- Decision register: <on (Medium and Large) | off (Small)> — docs/decisions/, an index loaded every session and one file per area, read on demand; turn it off if you don't want it
- Usage pause (option `usage-pause` of the protocol): off until you turn it on (pause dispatches near the plan's usage limit)
- Periodic agent review: off until you say yes; <weekly | from commit rhythm> when on
- Security posture: <pre-launch (guards only for production, real users' data, money or a hard constraint) | in production | off>
- Owner working style (items the environment does not settle), each off until you turn it on: <numbered item names from references/owner-working-style.md>
- Area practice options, each off until you turn it on: <the options of the proposed practices files, one line each>
- <other defaults>

Files
- create docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md
- create docs/practices/<area>.md  (one line per practices file)
- create docs/decisions/INDEX.md, resources.md, history.md, <area>.md  (only when the register is on; one area file per justified area)
- create .claude/agents/<name>.md  (one line per agent)
- create|change CLAUDE.md — adds the "Operating model" pointer section
```

1	<!--
2	Template for docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md. Fill every {{placeholder}}; delete these comments.
3	Write it in the owner's language (headings included). For a Small-tier project, remove
4	the Leads row, the Areas table's Lead column, the Lead rotation rule and lead-specific lines.
5	When headings are translated, update the in-file anchors (#report-format-…, #the-hand-back-script) and the
6	"§ <section>" names cited in the agent files, the practices files and the CLAUDE.md pointer
7	to match. Drop the docs/practices paragraph under Areas when no practices file was approved.
8	Values marked "default — tune" are starting values the owner adjusts. A section marked
9	"(optional)" stays only when the proposal's editable default turned it on; a line marked
10	"(option: <name>)" stays, without the mark, only when that option is on.
11	-->
12	
13	# {{Project}} — Operating model
14	
15	{{Project}} is built by an agent organization running in Claude Code for {{owner: one person | a team}}. This file is the protocol every agent follows. The main session, every lead and every specialist read it first.
16	
17	## Chain of command
18	
19	| Role | Who | Defined in | Talks to |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| **Owner** | {{owner}} | — | The main session |
22	| **Main session ("CEO")** | The main Claude Code session in this repo | `CLAUDE.md` + this file | The owner, the leads and the one-task executors it spawns |
23	| **Leads** | One per area | `.claude/agents/{{lead-prefix}}-*.md` | The main session (report) and their specialists |
24	| **Specialists** | Reusable experts per task type | `.claude/agents/{{specialist-prefix}}-*.md` | Whoever spawned them (report) |
25	| **Team members** | Ad-hoc implementers and reviewers spawned for one task | The spawn prompt | Whoever spawned them (report) |
26	
27	### Areas
28	
29	| Area | Lead | Specialists | Signal |
30	|---|---|---|---|
31	| {{area}} | `{{lead}}` | `{{specialist}}`, … | `{{path}}` |
32	
33	How agents work on each kind of thing lives in `docs/practices/`: {{`ui.md` (screens), `backend.md` (APIs and data), … — one entry per practices file}}. The lead of an area reads its file first; a specialist reads the sections its brief names; reviewers judge by the whole file.
34	
35	## Models and effort
36	
37	Every spawn sets `model` explicitly, and sets `effort` explicitly where the CLI supports the per-invocation parameter (Claude Code 2.1.292 or later). Otherwise the floor in the agent file applies. Models are named by alias, never by full ID.
38	
39	| Work | `model` | `effort` |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| Lookups and formatting | `sonnet` (or `haiku`, see below) | `low` |
42	| Mechanical work: routine edits, docs, config, ports a plan already defines — and its review | `sonnet` for the work, `opus` for the review | `medium` |
43	| Real logic, design | `opus` | `high` for logic; `medium` when a plan already holds the design |
44	| Fixes of review findings | as for the work | `medium` |
45	| Review where production personal data, money, auth or a hard constraint is at stake | `opus` | `high` |
46	| Leads | `opus` | `medium`, `high` for a hard area |
47	| Anything at `xhigh` or `max` | — | Only with the main session's explicit OK |
48	
49	- `haiku` with `low` only for a lookup whose answer can be checked, or for running a gate and summarizing its result. Never for logic, security, personal data, money, docs, reviews or leads. Its output is checked by a script or by its spawner before use; a lookup a script can answer needs no agent.
50	- **Before every spawn the main session answers two questions:** does the task need a coordinator (several agents or stop points) or one executor? Does it need new reasoning, or is it mechanical? The answers pick the row:
51	
52	  | Task | Agent | `model` | `effort` |
53	  |---|---|---|---|
54	  | A record, doc edit or summary from facts the brief holds | one executor (`<Area> › Executor`) | `sonnet` | `medium` |
55	  | A lookup or a gate run whose answer a script checks | one executor | `haiku` | `low` |
56	  | A plan's stop point, area work with several agents | the area's lead | `opus` | `medium` |
57	  | New logic, money, auth, personal data, a hard constraint, design | the area's lead | `opus` | `high` |
58	  | A review | a reviewer | `opus` | the reviewed task's |
59	- Each agent file carries a floor (`model`/`effort` in its frontmatter) for spawns that omit the parameters. The floor is a safety net, not the choice.
60	- Prefer resuming a finished agent with `SendMessage` over spawning a new one for the same thread of work.
61	- The main session evaluates and delegates (`CLAUDE.md`): it does a piece of work itself only when delegating it would block it, or would spend many tokens for nothing; research, extraction, measurement and analysis go to agents from the first step. It briefs, decides and checks. Its effort is never lowered to save tokens.
62	- **Titles.** The Agent tool's `description` is the title the owner sees in the agent list. It starts with who the agent is, a pipe, then the task: `<Role> | <task>` (an ad-hoc member: `<Area> › <role> | <task>`). A title can't change later and a resumed agent keeps it, so a lead is named for its role, not its first task. Leads title their own spawns the same way.
63	- **Waiting for children.** A lead waits for every child it spawned to return, and hands back with their work committed. A child resumed with `SendMessage` runs in the background, even when its first run was in the foreground: a lead that resumes a child and needs its result does not end its turn, and waits with one blocking command of at most 4 minutes 30 seconds (a shell until-loop capped at 270 s that ends on the child's commit or report, then the next such call, until the child ends; never `Monitor`, which returns at once and ends a subagent's turn). A subagent's prompt cache lasts about 5 minutes, so the turn after a longer wait writes its whole context into the cache again. A capped wait repeated is not polling; the main session is not held to the cap. If the lead is told to hand back while a child still runs, its report's status line is `BLOCKED: waiting for <child id>`, and the main session resumes the lead only after that child's notification.
64	- At each lead hand-back the main session runs [the hand-back script](#the-hand-back-script): a child of the lead that wrote to its transcript in the last 2 minutes still runs, and the report counts as `BLOCKED: waiting for <child id>`.
65	- Before integrating a lead's work into a shared checkout, the main session runs `git status`; uncommitted work there means it resumes the lead to finish it.
66	- **Lead rotation:** a lead is replaced by a fresh one at each plan stop point, or when its transcript passes about {{5 MB}} of conversation (its `user` and `assistant` records, image data stripped) or {{150}} model turns, whichever comes first. It is measured by [the hand-back script](#the-hand-back-script) at each hand-back and before each `SendMessage` resume. (default — tune)
67	
68	## Talking to the owner
69	
70	- Only the main session talks to the owner. {{Point at the owner-contact rules already in CLAUDE.md, if any; then list here the owner working style items the owner turned on.}}
71	- Before asking, the main session checks whether the docs already answer the question; if so, it answers itself and cites the file.
72	- A prompt meant for an outside tool (a paid generator, an external service) is shown to the owner and approved before it is sent; a change of wording goes back to the owner.
73	- Subagents cannot ask the owner. When they need a decision they stop at a safe point and end their report with a questions block. The main session asks the owner, then resumes the agent with `SendMessage`, passing the answers verbatim.
74	- Before acting in a browser where the owner is signed in, the main session says in one line the site, the element and the text it will type, and acts on the owner's yes.
75	
76	### Report format (every agent)
77	
78	Headings in {{language}}. The first line is the status, so the spawner can act on it before reading the rest:
79	
80	```
81	<DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED: <reason> | <reviewer verdict>>
82	## Report — <agent> — <task>
83	**Result:** <one line>
84	**Done:** <bullets>
85	**Evidence:** <commands run and what they returned, files>
86	**Skills invoked:** <list; a named skill skipped, and why>
87	**Files and commits:** <paths, commit hashes>
88	**Questions:**
89	1. <question> — context: <one line>; options: A (recommended) …, B …; blocking: yes/no; meanwhile: <what was done or skipped while waiting>
90	**Risks and next steps:** <bullets>
91	```
92	
93	Evidence, not assertions: anything not run is written as "not verified". Short lists, not prose.
94	
95	### When a permission check denies an action
96	
97	The agent stops that action: no rewording and retrying, no other tool for the same result (running it through a script runner counts as another tool), no handing it to another agent, no reading of permission or classifier settings. It finishes what does not depend on it and returns the denial's exact text to whoever spawned it.
98	
99	The main session reports to the owner the action, its purpose, the denial text and the likely cause. The owner picks the measure: a fresh agent with a clean context, the owner's own typed authorization naming the action, or a change of the session's permission mode, which only the owner makes. The denial's text is not copied into the brief of the agent dispatched next.
100	
101	**Live third-party accounts.** An action on a live third-party account (DNS, hostnames, tokens, billing, any account of the owner) runs only with the owner's typed authorization naming the command, collected before the dispatch, and by an agent spawned for it. An option picked from a multiple-choice question is not that authorization, and an agent is not resumed to widen it. This is the one case where the owner answers by typing a message, not by picking an option.
102	
103	## How work flows
104	
105	### The current design comes first
106	
107	Before the main session or a lead changes, fixes or dispatches work on anything (a feature, a page, a workflow, a rule), it reads that thing's approved design: its spec, its PRD, its scope's conventions and the owner's decisions recorded there. A problem is judged against that design first: what it says should happen, and whether the work drifted from it. A brief points the lead at that design, and the lead's report opens with what the design says and what the work changes.
108	
109	### Decisions and facts
110	
111	- Every decision in a spec or plan carries its provenance: (owner, with the option picked quoted verbatim and the date), (specialist's call), (approved design) or (proposed). A temporary rule states its start and "until the owner says otherwise"; a rule that replaces another names the one it replaces.
112	- An option's label is the owner's choice; its description is the main session's text. A decision records the label picked; any wording inside the description stays (proposed) until the owner sees it in place.
113	- A rule that limits the customer states its consequence for the customer and its provenance. A permanence word about the customer's data, names or money ("never", "forever", "irreversible") names the owner's words and date, or a reviewer fails it.
114	- A business or product plan is a hypothesis, not an implementation plan: a line of it enters a spec only with its consequence stated and the owner's yes; until then it is (proposed).
115	- Rejected options and the owner's accepted exceptions to a rule or standard are kept in one list per scope. No agent or reviewer "fixes" or reopens one without asking.
116	- An external fact (a price, a law, an API, a competitor's claim) carries its source and the date it was read, or "not verified". No done criterion rests on a fact from memory.
117	
118	### The decision register (optional)
119	
120	`docs/decisions/INDEX.md` (loaded every session, no decisions in it) points at one file per area and at `resources.md` (one row per domain, host, account, mailbox and key name: its role and what it must never be used for). Each entry: the decision, why, the owner's words with the date, and "irreversible after production" where it applies; a rule already in a conventions file is linked, not copied. A decision that replaces another moves the old entry to `history.md`.
121	
122	- The main session writes a new decision into its area file before the next step.
123	- A task reads its area's file first; a resource is used only after its row is read, and with no row the owner is asked.
124	- A spec, plan or runbook that contradicts the register, or uses a resource with no row, fails review.
125	
126	### Non-code work and milestones
127	
128	- Non-code work (copy, legal, research, design) runs as: brief → specialists draft → lead reviews → owner approves → saved in the repo. A draft holds nothing until approved.
129	- One milestone at a time, unless the owner asks otherwise. At its close, the roadmap and features docs are updated and the next step is reported as options.
130	
131	### Execution pace
132	
133	- **Fewer turns.** Every model call starts from a fixed base (the imported docs, tools and skills), so the number of turns is the cost. Batch independent tool calls in one message. Resume a finished agent on the same thread instead of spawning anew, until rotation calls for a fresh one. An agent reports once, at the end of its task. No polling by repeated calls: wait with one command that ends on the condition (a subagent's wait for a child is capped, as § Waiting for children says).
134	- **Dispatch only what the task needs.** One task of one kind of work goes to one specialist. Splitting agents by area and kind of work does not mean more spawns: never spawn every specialist of an area "for coverage".
135	- **Stop rule.** After two rounds in which the measured number does not move toward the goal, the agent stops and reports options; no third round without the main session's OK.
136	
137	### Briefs
138	
139	- A brief points at a rule or a plan section by its line range; it never copies it. Copies drift. A brief to a specialist names the sections of the practices files it needs the same way.
140	- A brief names the one or two skills the task requires, from the agent file's list.
141	- A brief never tells an agent to get around a tool's protection.
142	- A brief states the goal and what is ruled out, not a hypothesis: a brief that carries a hypothesis tends to come back confirmed.
143	- A brief passes an owner's choice with its intent and says what not to take literally. A question about a tone or a feeling names the effect in plain words, never a metaphor an agent could build literally.
144	- A brief gives a reviewer the owner's decisions as context, never as a list of what it must not look at.
145	- A brief ends with one line pointing at [Report format](#report-format-every-agent); that format replaces the report template of any other skill the agent runs.
146	{{- If CLAUDE.md has shell or file-reading rules: "A brief points at <that rule> and does not restate it."}}
147	
148	### Review cadence
149	
150	- **One owner each:** a lead owns exactly one area and a specialist does one kind of work. New work outside every agent's scope gets a new agent, not a wider one.
151	- **Adversarial review of domain work** runs in the area that owns it: a fresh instance of that area's lead, plus specialists who did not write the work. It never goes to the quality lead or reviewer.
152	- **Per task, by risk:** a read-only reviewer per task where production personal data, money, auth or a hard constraint is involved (test data in local or staging does not count). Low-risk tracks get one reviewer per group of tasks.
153	- A finding that is only wording is fixed directly, without a new review round.

10	
11	Some apps start a new session from a card that can end up nested under the session that created it. The protocol says the next main session is a new top-level session; in such an app, the incoming session checks where it sits and moves itself to the top level before taking over. 13	## The hand-back script
14	
15	The protocol's § Session hygiene holds this script (Step 5 writes it there, with the project's folder filled in): the main session runs it at every lead hand-back. It depends on Claude Code's transcript layout (`~/.claude/projects/<project-dir>/<session>.jsonl`, the session's subagents under `<session>/subagents/` with a `.meta.json` naming `parentAgentId`), checked in one project; re-check it after a Claude Code update. `<project-dir>` is the folder Claude Code uses for the repo there (its absolute path with `/` replaced by `-`). Size counts only the `user` and `assistant` records, image data stripped: the app's own records add megabytes to every session whatever its length. A child that wrote in the last 2 minutes still runs.
16	
17	```sh
18	python3 - <project-dir> <session> [<lead-agent-id>] <<'EOF'
19	import json,glob,os,re,sys,time
20	LIMIT=5e6  # rotation threshold in bytes of conversation (default — tune)
21	base=os.path.expanduser(f'~/.claude/projects/{sys.argv[1]}/{sys.argv[2]}')
22	lead=sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv)>3 else None
23	def size(p):
24	    b=0;ids=set()
25	    for l in open(p):
26	        try: d=json.loads(l)
27	        except ValueError: continue
28	        if d.get('type') in ('user','assistant'): b+=len(re.sub(r'"data":"[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{200,}"','',l).encode())
29	        m=d.get('message') or {}
30	        if m.get('role')=='assistant' and m.get('id'): ids.add(m['id'])
31	    return f'{b/1e6:.1f} MB of conversation, {len(ids)} turns'+(' -> rotate at the next clean point' if b>LIMIT else '')
32	if lead:
33	    for m in glob.glob(f'{base}/subagents/*.meta.json'):
34	        if json.load(open(m)).get('parentAgentId')!=lead: continue
35	        age=time.time()-os.path.getmtime(m.replace('.meta.json','.jsonl'))
36	        print(('WRITING ' if age<120 else 'idle ')+os.path.basename(m)[6:-10], int(age),'s')
